subject: CAIQ: control scope, residency clarification & parquet log sample request
messages:
From: Devon Hayes <devon.hayes@asteria-fin.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: security@asteria-fin.com
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: CAIQ: control mapping scope & log sample request

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for taking this — quick context: Asteria is running a routine cloud assurance review and our security team needs a CAIQ mapping focused on data residency, logging/telemetry, key management, and access reviews for the Redwood environment that will host PII-derived vectors.

Can you confirm:
- Which parts of Redwood are in-scope for CAIQ controls when a customer pins a model to dedicated capacity vs hosted?
- Residency: we need explicit coverage for customer data residency controls and whether logs/snapshots ever cross regions.
- Evidence: can you provide a small sample of telemetry logs in parquet format (sanitized/redacted) that demonstrates retention metadata and log lineage (request -> model id -> worker node)?

Deliverables we expect: CAIQ control crosswalk (mapping your control IDs to CSA questions), an owner roster for controls called out in the crosswalk, and a 1–2 small parquet log files with PII redacted. We do not need full datasets — just samples and the extraction steps so our auditors can replicate.

Timeline: is a 3 business day turnaround reasonable for the crosswalk and a redacted sample? If not, please propose an ETA. Also please list any controls that will require legal or product review before we can share artifacts.

Appreciate it — we can schedule a short follow-up call if that helps.

Thanks,
Devon Hayes
Security Engineer
Asteria Financial
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Devon Hayes <devon.hayes@asteria-fin.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 10:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: CAIQ: control mapping scope & log sample request

Devon — thanks for the clear ask.

Short answers up front:
- Scope: when a customer pins a model to Redwood Dedicated, the Dedicated environment (GPU pools, VPC peering where configured, and associated control plane pieces) is in-scope. For hosted API usage, the hosted control plane and multi-tenant inference runtime will be the relevant scope. We can annotate the CAIQ crosswalk with those scope boundaries per control (e.g., CCM-logging controls will have different evidence sources for Dedicated vs Hosted).
- Residency: logs tied to model execution (trace logs, routing metadata) are stored in the region where the workload executes. We do not copy raw request payloads across regions without explicit crossover (e.g., customer-requested migration). We'll make this explicit in the crosswalk and include the retention policy references.
- Parquet samples: yes — we can provide redacted parquet samples that show request-id, model-id, node-id, timestamp, and retention metadata. We'll strip payload text and hash identifiers where necessary.

I propose the following timeline:
- Crosswalk draft (v1) + control owner roster: 48 business hours
- Parquet redacted sample + extraction steps: 72 business hours (to allow security review and PII redaction)

Controls that might need legal/product review prior to sharing are primarily those involving retention of payloads (we will not share raw prompts/outputs). We'll flag those in the crosswalk.

Next steps: Marissa, can you pick this up as the owner for assembling the crosswalk artifacts and coordinating redaction? Rishi, can you confirm the path and sample extraction for the parquet logs (S3 buckets and scrub pipeline)?

If helpful, I'll open a shared Drive folder and add the initial skeleton.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Manager, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

- Provide the extraction steps (CLI commands or runbook) so Asteria's auditors can reproduce locally against an anonymized dump.
- Also prepare the control_owner_roster.csv mapping control ids to owners (example rows: CCM-08 -> infra-ops@redwood.com).

Attachments I will upload to the shared folder and link in my next message:
- CAIQ_control_crosswalk_v1.xlsx (draft mapping + scope notes)
- control_owner_roster.csv (draft)
- parquet_sample_redacted.parquet.stub (placeholder — actual sample will be uploaded to Drive/S3 after security sign-off)

Thanks — I'll assemble the sample and the extraction runbook today. Quick operational notes:
- Source path: s3://redwood-telemetry-prod/<region>/execution-traces/2027/04/ (we'll copy a subset to s3://redwood-artifact-share/caiq-ast-347/ after redaction).
- Redaction steps: use the telemetry-scrub tool (v2.4) with flags --hash-ids --drop-payload --preserve-metadata. Example: telemetry-scrub --input s3://... --output ./parquet_sample_redacted.parquet --format parquet --fields request_id,model_id,node_id,timestamp,retention_flag,source_tag.
- Control owners (preview): CCM-03 -> infra-ops@redwood.com; CCM-10 -> platform-sec@redwood.com; CCM-18 -> compliance@redwood.com. I'll produce control_owner_roster.csv with full contact emails.
- ETA: crosswalk + roster (Marissa's draft) -> today EOD PDT; redacted parquet sample & runbook -> tomorrow EOD PDT (post security review).

I'll place artifacts in the Drive folder at: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cCAIQ_samples and will open view access to devon@asteria-fin.com after we get security sign-off. HubSpot ticket: HS-1284 tracks this request/discussion.
